about: D32 (decision log): the paired, interleaved confirmation that is the verdict on "no latency regression", run before the regeneration on the 300,000-patient snapshot this tree builds, by tools/benchmark_matcher.py --paired-confirm (protocol paired-interleaved-1.0) into a scratch report and committed here as it was written. The reference is main before D32 (7f5930e, extracted from git); the candidate is this tree, whose files the artifact digests bind. The replication is the paired_confirmation of verification/matcher-comparison-report.json. The confirmation queries carry no Nth occurrence or count, so this measures the path every earlier request takes.
rule: No latency regression: at 14 workers the paired p95 ratio (candidate over reference) is at most 1.05 in every one of the four pairs, and the candidate's own p95 over its 14-worker runs is at most 10 s, with the maximum at most 30 s and query-process memory under 4 GB; the 8-worker figures are reported (committed in 1317259).

paired_confirmation.order: ABBA: the reference first in even repeats, the candidate first in odd
paired_confirmation.note: Each pair is the reference code and the candidate code run back to back, each in a fresh process with a warm pool, on the same snapshot and queries; the reference runs first in even repeats and second in odd ones (ABBA). Ratios are candidate over reference: below 1 means the candidate is faster. "total" is the sum of the per-query match seconds of one run. The absolute target is judged on the candidate's own runs in this session. The pairing cancels drift that is slow against the length of a pair (minutes); it does not cancel noise within a run, nor a difference that only one order shows (compare the reference-first and candidate-first pairs).

limitations: one machine and one session; synthetic data replicated beyond 10,000 patients; the p95 of 30 queries is the second-slowest query; the paired protocol cancels slow drift, not noise inside a run
